messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] which likelihood function can fit positive non-integer？
parts:
It could also be that you should take the logarithm of your data and then do a Gaussian likelihood, as is sometimes done for biomass.

You can use model selection like dic, waic and cpo to get an understanding of which likelihoods are bad choices.

Haakon
